text.en: Two competing analyses bear on word-final vowel-plus-glide sequences in Hokkaido Ainu. Itabashi reports that the inventory and number of semivowels are identical across all dialects, with *y* and *w* as the relevant segments ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-inventory-and-number-of-semivowels-are-identical⟧. Murasaki asserts that /w/ is realized as [w] at syllable onset but weakens in syllable-coda position, so that careful speech yields [-uʔV] where rapid speech yields [-uwV] ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-glide-w-is-w-at-syllable-onset⟧; similarly, /y/ is [j] at syllable onset and weakens in coda position, with careful [-Vʔi] becoming [-Vy] in rapid speech ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-glide-y-is-j-at-syllable-onset⟧.
text.ja: 北海道アイヌ語における語末の母音＋滑音連続については、二つの競合する分析が存在する。Itabashiは、半母音の種類と数はどの方言も全く同じであり、*y*と*w*が該当する分節音であると報告している⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-inventory-and-number-of-semivowels-are-identical⟧。Murasakiは、/w/は音節頭では[w]として実現されるが音節末では弱くなり、丁寧な発音では[-uʔV]、早い発音では[-uwV]となると主張する⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-glide-w-is-w-at-syllable-onset⟧。同様に、/y/は音節頭では[j]であり音節末では弱くなり、丁寧な[-Vʔi]が早い発音では[-Vy]となるとされる⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-glide-y-is-j-at-syllable-onset⟧。

text.en: The consonant analysis holds that post-vocalic *y* and *w* function as coda consonants rather than as vowels or epenthetic segments. Nakagawa asserts that phonetically /-y/ is almost identical to [i], but phonologically it behaves as a consonant that forms a single syllable with the preceding vowel, cannot bear accent, and is pronounced more weakly than /i/, as in *aynu* and *kamuy* ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--phonetically-y-is-almost-identical-to-i-but⟧; the same holds for /-w/, which is phonetically almost identical to [u] but phonologically a consonant forming a single syllable with the preceding vowel, unable to bear accent and pronounced more weakly than /u/, as in *ohaw* and *kewtum* ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--phonetically-w-is-almost-identical-to-u-but⟧. A transitional glide between vowels is not a phoneme, so non-phonemic [y] and [w] appearing between vowels are not written in phonemic transcription ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--a-transitional-glide-watari-between-vowels-is-not⟧; for example, the [y] in [iyomante], from prefix /i-/ and verb /omante/, and the [w] in [uwenewsar], from prefixes /u-/ and /e-/ and verb /newsar/, are non-phonemic and are transcribed phonemically as /iomante/ and /uenewsar/ ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-transitional-y-in-iyomante-from-prefix-i⟧. By contrast, the [w] in /iwor/ 'hunting ground' is the realization of the phoneme /w/ and not a transitional glide ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-w-in-iwor-hunting-ground-is-the⟧, and the word for 'eloquence' has the stem /paw/ rather than *pa* with an epenthetic glide, meaning there are two roots for 'mouth', /pa/ and /paw/ ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-word-for-eloquence-has-the-stem-paw⟧. The phonemic form of the verb for 'to hurt' in the Chitose and Saru dialects is /iunin/, and the phonetic [y] in [iyunin] is a transitional glide rather than a phoneme ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-phonemic-form-of-the-verb-for-to⟧. Murasaki reports semivocalization in clusters such as *-n + s-* becoming *-ys-*, *-V + 'i-* becoming *-Vy-*, *-V + 'u-* becoming *-Vw-*, *-V + 'a* becoming *-Vya-*, and *'u + 'V-* becoming *-wVV-* ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--semivowelization-occurs-in-clusters-such-as-n-s⟧. In the *y*:*w* consonant alternation, Yakumo characteristically takes *w* where other dialects take *y*, and Horobetsu and Obihiro take *y* where other dialects take *w*, as seen in *puyár* / *puwár* and *suyóp* / *suwóp* ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--in-the-y-w-consonant-alternation-yakumo-characteristically⟧.
text.ja: 子音分析においては、母音後の*y*と*w*は母音や挿入音ではなく末子音として機能するとされる。Nakagawaは、/-y/は発音上ほとんど[i]と同じであるが、音韻論的には子音として扱われ、前の母音と一つの音節を形成し、アクセントが載らず、/i/より弱く発音されると主張し、*aynu*や*kamuy*をその例として挙げる⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--phonetically-y-is-almost-identical-to-i-but⟧。同様に、/-w/は発音上ほとんど[u]と同じであるが、音韻論的には子音として前の母音と一つの音節を形成し、アクセントが載らず、/u/より弱く発音されるとされ、*ohaw*や*kewtum*がその例である⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--phonetically-w-is-almost-identical-to-u-but⟧。母音間に生じるわたりは音素ではないため、母音間に現れる非音素的な[y]や[w]は音韻表記されない⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--a-transitional-glide-watari-between-vowels-is-not⟧。たとえば、接頭辞/i-/と動詞/omante/からなる[iyomante]の[y]、および接頭辞/u-/・/e-/と動詞/newsar/からなる[uwenewsar]の[w]はわたり音であり、音韻的にはそれぞれ/iomante/、/uenewsar/と表記される⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-transitional-y-in-iyomante-from-prefix-i⟧。これに対し、「猟場」を表す/iwor/の[w]は音素/w/の実現であってわたりではなく⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-w-in-iwor-hunting-ground-is-the⟧、「雄弁」の語幹はわたりを伴う*pa*ではなく/paw/であり、「口」の語根として/pa/と/paw/の二つが存在するとされる⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-word-for-eloquence-has-the-stem-paw⟧。千歳・沙流方言において「痛む」という動詞の音韻形は/iunin/であり、[iyunin]の[y]は音素ではなくわたり音である⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-phonemic-form-of-the-verb-for-to⟧。Murasakiは、*-n + s-*が*-ys-*に、*-V + 'i-*が*-Vy-*に、*-V + 'u-*が*-Vw-*に、*-V + 'a*が*-Vya-*に、*'u + 'V-*が*-wVV-*になる半母音化を報告している⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--semivowelization-occurs-in-clusters-such-as-n-s⟧。子音交替*y*:*w*においては、他方言が*y*を持つところで八雲が*w*を持ち、他方言が*w*を持つところで幌別と帯広が*y*を持つことが特徴的であり、*puyár* / *puwár*や*suyóp* / *suwóp*にその例が見られる⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--in-the-y-w-consonant-alternation-yakumo-characteristically⟧。

text.en: Bugaeva asserts that when the prefixes *i-* (indefinite object) or *u-* (reciprocal) occur intervocalically in an accent-bearing position, they turn into a glide and form a syllable with the following vowel ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--when-the-prefixes-i-indefinite-object-or-u⟧.
text.ja: Bugaevaは、接頭辞*i-*（不定目的語）または*u-*（相互）がアクセント担持位置で母音間に現れる場合、半母音化して後続母音と一つの音節を形成すると主張する⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--when-the-prefixes-i-indefinite-object-or-u⟧。

text.en: Early researchers generally analyzed word-final vowel-plus-glide sequences as diphthongs. Kindaichi and Chiri assert that diphthongs include *ai*, *ui*, *oi*, *au*, *iu*, *eu*, *ou*, *ei*, and *ae*, all of which are falling diphthongs ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--diphthongs-include-ai-ui-oi-au-iu-eu⟧; among these, *ou*, *ei*, and *ae* are extremely rare, with *ou* occurring only in *kokou* 'son-in-law', *ei* formed when short *e* is emphasized, and *ae* occurring only word-initially through rapid contraction of *a-* and *e-* ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--among-diphthongs-ou-ei-and-ae-are-extremely⟧. Refsing asserts that in syllable-final position, semivowels /w/ and /y/ are realized as [u] and [i], forming diphthongs with the preceding vowel ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--coda-glides-form-diphthongs⟧, and further that when an unstressed /u/ or /i/ follows a vowel in the Shizunai dialect, it may be realized as non-syllabic [w] and [y] respectively ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--when-an-unstressed-u-or-i-follows-a⟧. Itabashi asserts that in Hokkaido Ainu the semivowels /y, w/ serve as the second vowel of a diphthong in syllable-coda position ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--in-hokkaido-ainu-the-semivowels-y-w-serve⟧, and makes the same claim for Sakhalin Ainu ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-semivowels-y-and-w⟧ and Kuril Ainu ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--in-kuril-ainu-y-and-w-in-syllable⟧. Shibatani asserts that diphthongs such as *ai*, *ui*, and *au* involve devocalization of the second vowel, yielding pronunciations [aj], [uj], and [aw] ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--diphthongs-such-as-ai-ui-and-au-involve⟧. Satō asserts that *y* and *w* can occur in syllable-coda position as well as onset position ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-glides-y-and-w-can-occur-in⟧, and that words such as *nay* and *haw* are monosyllabic, with *y* and *w* pronounced lightly and briefly following the vowel ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--words-such-as-nay-and-haw-are-monosyllabic⟧.
text.ja: 初期の研究者たちは一般に、語末の母音＋滑音連続を二重母音として分析した。KindaichiとChiriは、二重母音には*ai*、*ui*、*oi*、*au*、*iu*、*eu*、*ou*、*ei*、*ae*等があり、すべて下降式であると主張する⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--diphthongs-include-ai-ui-oi-au-iu-eu⟧。このうち*ou*、*ei*、*ae*の用例は極めて少なく、*ou*は*kokou*（婿）のみ、*ei*は短母音*e*の強調時に成立し、*ae*は語頭で*a-*と*e-*の結合が急言された場合にのみ成立するとされる⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--among-diphthongs-ou-ei-and-ae-are-extremely⟧。Refsingは、音節末尾において半母音/w/と/y/は[u]および[i]として実現され、先行する母音とともに二重母音を形成すると主張し⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--coda-glides-form-diphthongs⟧、さらに静内方言において無強勢の/u/または/i/が母音の後に続く場合、それぞれ非音節的な[w]および[y]に置き換えられることがあると述べる⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--when-an-unstressed-u-or-i-follows-a⟧。Itabashiは、北海道アイヌ語において半母音/y, w/は音節末では二重母音の第二母音となると主張し⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--in-hokkaido-ainu-the-semivowels-y-w-serve⟧、同様の主張を樺太アイヌ語⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--in-sakhalin-ainu-the-semivowels-y-and-w⟧および千島アイヌ語⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--in-kuril-ainu-y-and-w-in-syllable⟧についても行っている。Shibataniは、*ai*、*ui*、*au*などの二重母音は後半の母音の非音節化を伴い、[aj]、[uj]、[aw]のように発音されると主張する⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--diphthongs-such-as-ai-ui-and-au-involve⟧。Satōは、*y*と*w*は音節頭だけでなく音節末にも現れうると述べ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-glides-y-and-w-can-occur-in⟧、*nay*や*haw*のような語は一音節であり、*y*や*w*は母音に添えて軽く短く発音されると主張する⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--words-such-as-nay-and-haw-are-monosyllabic⟧。

text.en: Itabashi asserts that in Kuril Ainu, word-initial /y/ hardly ever occurs, and when it does, other records almost always transcribe it with another vowel ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--in-kuril-ainu-word-initial-y-hardly-ever⟧. Satō asserts that although *ku-ipe* can be theoretically assumed as the base form, its actual pronunciation is *ku-ype* ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--although-ku-ipe-can-be-theoretically-assumed-as⟧.
text.ja: Itabashiは、千島アイヌ語において語頭に/y/が現れるものはほとんどなく、現れた場合でも他の母音で表されたものが同時に記されていることがほとんどであると主張する⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--in-kuril-ainu-word-initial-y-hardly-ever⟧。Satōは、理論的には*ku-ipe*という形が基本形として仮定できるが、実際の発音では*ku-ype*となると述べる⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--although-ku-ipe-can-be-theoretically-assumed-as⟧。

text.en: Shibatani asserts that the semivowels /w/ and /y/ do not occur before [u] and [i] respectively, so the sequences [wu] and [ji] do not occur in Ainu ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-semivowels-w-and-y-do-not-occur⟧.
text.ja: Shibataniは、半母音/w/と/y/はそれぞれ[u]および[i]の前には生起せず、したがって連続[wu]と[ji]はアイヌ語に現れないと主張する⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--the-semivowels-w-and-y-do-not-occur⟧。

text.en: Murasaki reports several boundary-derived alternations in Sakhalin Ainu: initial *y-* is deleted following a coda *-n* ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--initial-y-is-deleted-following-a-coda-n⟧; initial *y-* drops after *-m* or *-s*, and initial *w-* assimilates to a preceding *-m* ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--initial-y-drops-after-m-or-s-and⟧; and initial *y-* alternates to *-n-* after coda *-h* ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--initial-y-alternates-to-n-after-coda-h⟧. Nakagawa asserts that when another element precedes a word beginning with vowels *i* or *u*, vowel weakening can occur, shifting *i* → *y* and *u* → *w* ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--when-another-element-precedes-a-word-beginning-with⟧, and that this process is frequently observed in the Saru and Chitose dialects ⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--vowel-weakening-i-y-u-w-is-frequently⟧.
text.ja: Murasakiは樺太アイヌ語において複数の境界由来の交替を報告している。語末子音*-n*に後続する語頭の*y-*は消去され⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--initial-y-is-deleted-following-a-coda-n⟧、*-m*や*-s*の後で語頭の*y-*が消失し、また*-m*の後で語頭の*w-*が同化する⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--initial-y-drops-after-m-or-s-and⟧。さらに語末の*-h*の後で語頭の*y-*は*-n-*に交替する⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--initial-y-alternates-to-n-after-coda-h⟧。Nakagawaは、母音*i*または*u*で始まる語の前に別の要素が来ると、母音弱化により*i* → *y*、*u* → *w*のように変化する現象があると主張し⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--when-another-element-precedes-a-word-beginning-with⟧、この母音弱化は沙流・千歳方言でよく見られると述べる⟦claim:phon/glides-w-y--vowel-weakening-i-y-u-w-is-frequently⟧。
